title: TypeScript SDK: output-contract tooling for union mapping and Zod/JSON-Schema interoperability
creator: Ava Chen
acceptance_criteria: Generator emits contract-meta.json for at least two TypeGen outputs
fromMetaToZod produces Zod schemas that match generated TS types
streamingResolver identifies discriminant within 128 tokens in >95% of tests
JSON-Schema export validates with ajv and round-trips for simple shapes
Docs + migration guide with 3 examples merged
implementation_notes: Create package @redwood/tsdk/out-contracts with modular entrypoints: index, zod, jsonschema, streaming
Keep runtime helpers tree-shakeable — export tiny helpers rather than large monoliths
Use a small incremental tokenizer heuristic for streamingResolver (prefix-scanner keyed to discriminator strings)
Bundle size target: <10KB (minified gzipped) for core helpers without Zod; with Zod opt-in
tests: unit: fromMetaToZod basic shapes (objects, arrays, optionals, enums)
integration: roundtrip types -> meta -> zod -> ajv JSON-Schema
streaming: synthetic token streams covering early/late discriminants and malformed outputs
e2e: console playground using dogfood prompts to ensure runtime doesn't block UI
comments: 2025-02-15 - Priya Kapoor (PM): Please prioritise streaming ergonomics; customers hit buffer-induced latencies. Also want sample for function-calling shaped outputs.

2025-02-20 - Noah Brooks (ASSIGNEE): Spike done — prototyped streamingResolver using a byte-prefix scan; accuracy at ~97% on internal prompt set. Pushed prototype to GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/tsdk/pull/312
2025-02-24 - Design review (Liam Martinez): API looks fine; suggest `resolveUnionStream` return explicit backpressure signals to integrate with UI consumers.
2025-02-28 - Security (Amina Shah): confirmed no secrets in metadata. Recommend opt-in telemetry for resolver metrics.
2025-03-02 - Code review (Sarah Voss): left comments on streaming step API, prefer `peek` + `consume` pair for clearer semantics. Minor nit on error types.
